title: Exercise Assurance inject commitment (public object)
description: Public, signed commitment to a sealed inject package. A hash commitment requires BINDING (EA cannot substitute a different package after committing) and HIDING (White cannot enumerate likely packages before reveal). Hiding comes from secret randomness withheld until reveal - see aegis.inject-opening.v2.

SUPERSEDES.status: DEPRECATED - DOES NOT PROVIDE PACKAGE HIDING. Do not use.
defects: The nonce was published in the signed public object, so it could provide uniqueness but no hiding. Randomness only defeats enumeration when the attacker does not already know it.
WORSE: the nonce was not included in the digest preimage at all. package_digest was SHA-384 over the canonical package only, so the nonce contributed nothing to binding either.
The v1 field description asserted that the nonce 'prevents a low-entropy package being brute-forced from its digest' - a security property the construction did not implement.
Inject packages are short and structurally predictable, so an unhidden commitment is enumerable in practice, not only in theory.
SUPERSEDES.reason_not_used: Program state is PREREQUISITES_PENDING / NOT_ASSESSMENT_READY; no exercise has been authorized.

commitment_construction.encoding_note: Use an unambiguous LENGTH-FRAMED preimage, never raw concatenation. Raw concatenation admits boundary-shifting between adjacent fields.
commitment_construction.length_encoding: 8-byte big-endian unsigned integer, byte length of the UTF-8 / raw octets that follow
commitment_construction.at_commitment: Publish this signed object. Withhold the package AND the opening_salt.
commitment_construction.at_reveal: EA publishes the package and the opening_salt; White recomputes c and compares.

field_disposition.commitment_digest: PUBLISHED  - binds the package and the secret opening value
field_disposition.public_nonce: OPTIONAL   - replay/correlation uniqueness ONLY. Provides NO hiding. Never rely on it for hiding.
field_disposition.opening_salt: WITHHELD   - prevents enumeration of possible inject packages
field_disposition.opening_salt + package: REVEALED at reveal - opens and verifies the commitment

type.description: Domain separation. Inside the signed payload.

commitment_digest.description: SHA-384 over the LENGTH-FRAMED preimage (domain || canonical_package || opening_salt).

reveal_deadline.description: After this, an unrevealed package is VOID, not pending.

public_nonce.description: OPTIONAL. Replay/correlation uniqueness only. NOT a hiding mechanism.

previous_commitment.description: commitment_id of the superseded commitment. Append-only chain.

signature.description: EA signature over the JCS canonicalization of every public field except 'signature'.

verification_sequence: 2.  Verify the EA signature over every public field except 'signature'.
3.  Confirm type, exercise_id, key ID, algorithm, and validity window.
4.  Confirm the commitment was published BEFORE exercise execution.
5.  Confirm the opening uses the expected package schema (aegis.inject-package.v1).
6.  Canonicalize the revealed package using the declared algorithm (JCS).
8.  Recompute the digest and CONSTANT-TIME compare.
9.  Validate inject identifiers, count, ordering rules, and timestamps.
11. Confirm the opening_salt has not appeared in any other commitment.
12. Preserve the commitment, opening, package, and verification result as evidence.
operational_requirements: opening_salt: 32 or 48 bytes from a CSPRNG. Never reused across commitments. Requires a salt registry to satisfy verification step 11.
EA must BACK UP the opening material. Losing the salt makes the commitment permanently unopenable - an availability failure that looks identical to refusal to reveal.
A changed package requires a NEW signed commitment with an explicit supersession_reason. Never overwrite. Both remain published and chained.
A supersession created after exercise start is itself a finding, reported under EA-6.
Any verification failure invalidates the inject package and is reported under EA-6.
